title: Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope for Waste Flow
description: Correct pipe pitch is vital for solid and liquid waste transport in gravity drainage systems. If the slope is too flat, standing water leads to grease accumulation and frequent blockages. Conversely, an excessive slope allows liquids to run off too quickly, leaving solid waste stranded in the line. Regular maintenance includes inspecting pipe hangers for sagging or displacement that creates low spots, known as belly lines. Verifying uniform grade along horizontal branch drains ensures self-scouring velocity and prevents chronic clogs in residential and commercial waste piping.

Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope for Waste Flow

Conversely, an excessive slope allows liquids to run off too quickly, leaving solid waste stranded in the line. Regular maintenance includes inspecting pipe hangers for sagging or displacement that creates low spots, known as belly lines. Verifying uniform grade along horizontal branch drains ensures self-scouring velocity and prevents chronic clogs in residential and commercial waste piping.
